name: Pisco PAE versus sham
question: Does prostatic artery embolisation improve symptoms more than a sham catheter procedure in men with severe LUTS/BPH despite alpha-blocker treatment?

arms.label: Prostatic artery embolisation with 300–500 μm Bead Block particles
sham prostatic artery catheterisation without embolisation

design.population: 80 men older than 45 years with severe LUTS/BPH despite at least six months of alpha-blocker treatment, IPSS at least 20, QoL at least 3, Qmax below 12 mL/s, prostate volume at least 40 cm³, and catheterisation of a prostatic artery feasible before randomisation.
design.description: Single-centre, patient-blinded, sham-controlled superiority randomized trial

verdictNote: Both coprimary outcomes favored embolisation at six months; sham participants then crossed over.
takeaway: Prostatic artery embolisation with 300–500 μm particles improved six-month IPSS and quality-of-life scores more than sham catheterisation without embolisation in men with severe LUTS/BPH despite alpha-blockers; both prespecified coprimary superiority tests were met.

reports.label: Six-month blinded and 12-month crossover report
reports.citation: Pisco JM, Bilhim T, Costa NV, et al. "Randomised Clinical Trial of Prostatic Artery Embolisation Versus a Sham Procedure for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *Eur Urol.* 2020;77(3):354-362. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2019.11.010
reports.followUp: Six-month blinded comparison; open crossover and observation to 12 months

results.measure: Six-month mean IPSS change in points; adjusted mean difference, PAE minus sham
results.note: Intention-to-treat ANCOVA adjusted for baseline IPSS; first test in serial gatekeeper at two-sided alpha 0.05.
results.locator: Journal p359, Results; p360, Table 2; p356, Statistical analysis

results.measure: Six-month mean QoL score; mean difference, PAE minus sham
results.note: Coprimary t test passed after the IPSS gate; paper expresses the difference as sham minus PAE, +2.13 (95% CI 1.57–2.68).
results.locator: Journal p359, Results; p356, Statistical analysis

results.measure: Six-month mean change in maximum flow, mL/s; adjusted mean difference, PAE minus sham
results.note: Confidence interval and P value adjusted for multiple secondary comparisons.
results.locator: Journal p360, Table 2 and footnote a

results.measure: Six-month mean PVR change, mL; adjusted mean difference, PAE minus sham
results.note: Confidence interval and P value adjusted for multiple secondary comparisons.
results.locator: Journal p360, Table 2 and footnote a

results.measure: Mean IPSS improvement during six-month open crossover period
results.note: Within-group change in former sham arm after PAE; no concurrent sham comparison.
results.locator: Journal p354, Abstract, Results; p359, Results

harms.label: Any adverse event during blinded period
harms.note: Sixteen events after randomized PAE and 17 after sham.

harms.label: Clavien–Dindo IIIa event after crossover PAE

values.ctl: 1/38 (2.6%) former sham participants after crossover PAE

harms.note: Expelled prostatic fragments caused haematuria and acute retention, treated with TURP; not an event in the randomized blinded PAE arm.

delivery.label: Bilateral embolisation in randomized PAE arm
Tamsulosin at six months among evaluable patients
delivery.note: Treatment could be stopped after symptom improvement by study physician; denominators inferred from the reported counts and percentages.
